findings.breaking_input: After `pair ex1 --from a --to d ...` has run and variant-d exists, the composer (or any later step) runs `rm docs/design/explore/ex1/pairs.json` or renames it. Then `compose-done`, `surfaces` and the coverage gate run with VARIANTS="a b c". Variant-d, the high-judgment arm, ships with no surface markers and no render coverage, and the script prints "3 of 3".
findings.why: The set of gated variants is switched on by `[ -f pairs.json ]`, a file the guarded party can delete. The patch re-creates the exact hole it set out to close, just one step further out. Nothing cross-checks the variant-* directories on disk or the seal against the pair list.
findings.fix: Key the guard on the committed record: the seal, or the variant-* directories that exist. If pairs.json is missing while the seal or any variant-[d-z] directory exists, refuse. Alternatively, record the pairs in the sealed record and read them from there.
findings.twin_of: A guard switched on by the presence of a file the guarded party can delete -> key the guard on the committed record (the seal), and refuse when its companion is missing

findings.breaking_input: A pairs.json written by a different serializer, such as `"to" : "d"` (space before the colon), `"to":\t"d"` (tab), or a pretty-printer that puts the value on the next line. The grep pattern `"to": *"[a-z]"` allows only spaces after the colon and nothing before it, so it matches nothing. VARIANTS stays "a b c" and no error is raised.
findings.why: This is a textual grep of a JSON file, not a parse. Any formatting variation silently becomes "no pairs". An absent match is read as "not applicable" instead of a failure, and a pair that exists is never gated.
findings.fix: Parse with node, which the lane already uses (design-expa1.mjs), and fail when the file is non-empty but yields zero `to` entries. Cross-check that the count of parsed entries equals the count of `"to"` occurrences.
findings.twin_of: A failing probe command read as "not applicable" -> only a positive "absent" skips; an error is a failure.

findings.breaking_input: pairs.json that is unreadable (permission denied), truncated, or contains a NUL byte. The grep exit status is discarded inside `$(...)`, and GNU grep prints "Binary file matches" for a binary file instead of a match. The loop gets an empty word list or junk, and VARIANTS is left as "a b c" with no warning.
findings.why: The status of the grep and cut pipeline is never read, so a failed read looks the same as a pairs.json with zero pairs. The result is fail-open.
findings.fix: Capture the output into a variable inside a conditional and check the status. Refuse when the file exists but cannot be read or parsed. Use `grep -a`, or parse with node and exit non-zero on a throw.
findings.twin_of: A subprocess result was ignored -> read status and error of every spawn whose failure matters.

findings.breaking_input: Revert the fix so that only the `surfaces` loop uses a hard-coded list, or break the compose-done and render-coverage paths. The new test would still pass if `surfaces` alone reads the pair list.
findings.why: The bug being fixed was in compose-done ("printed 3 of 3"). The test exercises only `surfaces`, and it asserts "across 2 variant(s)" without ever running compose-done, self-review or coverage with a paired d. It has no control for a deleted or reformatted pairs.json (B1, B2), so the regression is not pinned where it occurred.
findings.fix: Add tests that run `compose-done` on a paired d and assert that d is named and counted as "N of 4". Add tests where pairs.json is deleted after the pair is made, and where it is reformatted. Both must refuse.
findings.twin_of: A refusal test aimed at a path another rule already refuses -> aim a gate's test where only that gate can refuse, and assert its reason.

findings.breaking_input: pairs.json that holds `"to": "d"` twice (pairs a→d and b→d), or a `"to": "z"` entry nested in an unrelated object. Duplicates are silently deduplicated. A key named "to" outside a pair row is added to VARIANTS as a gated variant.
findings.why: The `to` values are not validated against the pair command's grammar, and the pair rows are not counted. A duplicate target, or a stray key, changes the gated set without any refusal, and the dedup hides it.
findings.fix: Parse the pair rows structurally. Require each `to` to be unique, distinct from every `from`, and to match the same id grammar the `pair` command enforces. Refuse on any violation.
findings.twin_of: `find()` took the first of duplicate rows -> count matches; exactly one or refuse.
